lines.buy: 5 1/4 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced lengthwise into tenders
lines.notes: Corrected from the pre-resolve's 400 g: the line states its own weight, 1.5 lbs = 680 g. See macro_cross_check.

lines.buy: 3 1/2 tsp salt and 2 Tbsp black pepper, to taste
lines.notes: Salt reduced from the pre-resolve's 20 g default to 6 g source basis; 20 g over 4 servings is 5 g of added salt per serving, which no cook would use.

macro_cross_check: VERIFIED AND FOUND WRONG - there is a real each-weight defect on the main protein, exactly the failure rule 6 exists to catch, and I have corrected the gram basis. The precheck reports ours at 28 g protein against the source's 67.45 g, a 58% shortfall. Cause: the settled line 'Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast' carries 400 g source basis, derived from '2 medium' at 200 g each - but the line's own text states 1.5 lbs, which is 680 g. I reproduced the precheck exactly at 400 g (540 cal, 28.1 P) to confirm that is the driver, so this is not a guess. Corrected to 680 g the dish computes 351 cal / 38.1 P / 17.5 C per serving before tuning, and 170 g of raw breast per serving sits right on the catalog's own 167 g average across 80 live chicken-breast recipes. I have set grams_source 680 on that line. Note the source's published 67.45 g protein still looks like an outlier even after the fix - 680 g of raw breast cannot yield 270 g of protein - and most likely reflects a 2-serving nutrition basis in the source's markup; I would not chase our figures toward it. SEPARATE CONDITION BREACH, same cause as apple-spice-pork-chops: the precheck's tuning added a rice base of 200 g plus a further 50%, i.e. 75 g dry rice per serving, which alone contributes 60 g of carbohydrate. At 82.7 g carbs per serving (77.5 g on my corrected numbers) this fails the run's 35 g ceiling by more than double, while the dish itself is 17.5 g and passes easily. The rice base must be dropped or replaced before this ships.
